lessons: Take fliers before a third ground two-drop: my RG deck had almost no evasive finishers, and WR's fliers Chapel Geist and Gallows Warden were among the threats that beat me 0-2.
Tonight contradicted the guide: RG went 1-2 on 17 lands (9 Forest, 8 Mountain), not the 2-1 anecdote, and the extra land did not stop the losses.
Don't cut Army of the Damned and Endless Ranks of the Dead for a low curve; my games ran 25 to 41 turns, and my WB deck had too few late-game threats to close them out.
Value flyers and answers to flyers highly: Moon Heron and Stitched Drake were central to the UG deck that beat me 0-2 in round 3.
Prioritise removal like Claustrophobia over Liliana of the Veil; I lost 1-6 in games with a WB deck that had little answer to the threats I faced.
The guide's claim that ground decks stall was wrong for my BR: Dead Weight, Corpse Lunge and Stromkirk Patrol won 4 straight games against WR and RG, and only UR's fliers beat me.

Lost 0-2 to UR's Murder of Crows, Falkenrath Marauders and Invisible Stalker; my BR had only Vampire Interloper and Falkenrath Noble in the air, so take two more fliers before a third ground two-drop.
The guide's 16-land rule held: my 17-land BR stalled into a 33-turn win and a 24-turn loss, so with this low-curve small-creature list, play 16 lands, cutting a Swamp.
Count pips before cutting lands: my 10 Plains/7 Mountains left double-red Vampiric Fury and Into the Maw of Hell hard to cast; split red-heavy top-end evenly or cut it.
Games stalled: 33 and 41 turns in my long matches, so prioritise cheap evasive threats like Chapel Geist over slow top-end such as Galvanic Juggernaut.
Curse of Death's Hold (pick 1) and Mask of Avacyn (pick 8) went unplayed; from pick 1, prefer on-colour playables to speculative picks.
Once you take Victim of Night or Morkrut Banshee, stay black: I took Victim of Night first in pack 3, cut black for UG, and went 1-2 while the guide's black decks held up.
Tonight contradicted the guide's flier-first advice: my UG fliers (three Moon Heron, Stitched Drake) lost to WG's Smite the Monstrous and BG's Victim of Night, so take removal for fliers early.
My UG deck ran 17 lands and lost 25- and 28-turn games, so try 16 lands with a curve like this, though the guide's 16-land advice was not tested tonight.
Value evasive finishers over ground filler: my WG deck (8 Forest, 9 Plains) lost 21- and 20-turn games to BG and a 22-turn game to UR, stalling before Unburial Rites and Makeshift Mauler took over.
Don't overvalue pump tricks like Moment of Heroism and Ranger's Guile in a low-curve aggro deck; they won no games I can cite when my threats were stonewalled.
Keep removal like Smite the Monstrous and Bonds of Faith, but prioritize two-drop threats and card-advantage creatures in pack 2 to avoid long grinds.
Contradicting the guide, my BG deck ran 17 lands with two Walking Corpse and two Woodland Sleuth; try 16, since my 28-turn games suggest stalls.
My BG deck with Geistcatcher's Rig went 2-1 against UG's three Moon Herons, but UR's fliers and two Claustrophobia beat me 0-2, so keep two flier answers.
Stop taking off-colour fliers: I took Stitched Drake second in pack 2 and never played it, so favour on-colour evasion like Screeching Bat over blue speculation.
Blue removal was open late in pack 3: the second Claustrophobia came third pick, so take early removal and expect a second copy of Claustrophobia or Sensory Deprivation to wheel.
Three Makeshift Maulers, Murder of Crows, and Geistflame carried this 3-0 UR tempo deck, so prioritise efficient two- to four-drop bodies and cheap red burn in Innistrad.
The UR deck won 6-1 in games on 17 lands split 9 Island and 8 Mountain, so a two-colour tempo build with that split held up across three opponents.
